reasoning_traces.think:
Sympathy emerges as a probabilistic response to suffering, subject to modulation by competing instincts. The core mechanism operates through a Bayesian framework where prior beliefs about sympathy are updated in light of new instinctual stimuli. When inhibition thresholds are crossed—such as in the presence of hunting or pugnacious instincts—belief revision leads to near-zero sympathy probability. This is modeled as a stochastic process with deterministic breakdowns at critical instigation levels. Instinctual competition introduces nonlinearity into the system, where multiple drivers can suppress sympathy simultaneously. The emotional arousal threshold further governs whether a sympathetic response is enacted or suppressed. These dynamics form a closed-loop feedback system where evolutionary pressures shape both the structure of sympathy and its susceptibility to disruption.
